transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-27 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Torres (Silverline - Head of Search), Priya Nair (Silverline - ML), Olivia Park (Silverline PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll give a 2 minute intro then Samir will jump into the demo. can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Jared: yep, sounds good. we've got about 40 minutes.
[00:10] Maya: perfect. quick context - silverline is looking to improve product search relevance across web and mobile, priya sent over some examples of poor rerank, and jared mentioned cost concerns at scale. obvious use-case is embeddings + rerank with our hosted endpoints.
[00:25] Samir: cool, i'll share screen, show the embeddings call, how we build candidate vectors, then our rerank endpoint that takes query + candidates and returns scores and a re-ordered list.
[00:35] [screen share begins] Samir: first off here's the simple POST to /v1/embeddings, payload is text or batch of documents. we return a fixed-dim vector. small note - our hosted model catalog lists recommended models by throughput/cost. sometimes the auto-suggested model name is slightly different in the exports, transcription might show as redwood-ver-2, but it's the curated embedding family.
[01:05] Priya: what about chunking long product descriptions? we usually have long HTML fields.
[01:10] Samir: good q. we recommend semantic chunking at ~200 tokens, we show code samples in the Console; also prefix caching helps for repeated product info. chunking strategy note: you can store chunk vectors in your vector DB or use our embeddings storage paired with a fast ANN.
[01:30] Olivia: do you support partial update for product updates? we update inventory constantly.
[01:34] Samir: yes, incremental upserts are supported at the embeddings level. for rerank, you can push updated candidate vectors and only re-request rerank when query arrives - low latency path.
[01:50] Jared: can you walk the rerank flow with an example? we want to see where latency is spent.
[01:55] Samir: sure. step 1: client generates query embedding (POST embeddings). step 2: candidate retrieval from your ANN (we demo with Pinecone/FAISS in the sample). step 3: call Redwood /v1/rerank with raw query text + candidate texts or ids (we support both). we do pairwise scoring and return scores + final ordering. average rerank time in hosted tier is around 40-120ms for 10 candidates depending on model, seq len, and NVIDIA GPU type - want to emphasize that's a distribution.
[02:35] Jared: 40-120ms is ok for web, but mobile 200ms budget. what's realistic for 5 candidates?
[02:40] Samir: for 5 candidates you're typically in the 30-70ms window. we can also suggest a distilled reranker model or lower-dim embeddings to trade accuracy for latency. our Optimize tool will suggest batching and quantization profiles per workload.
[03:05] Priya: security - we can't send PII to hosted if retention policy isn't acceptable. do you have controls for data residency and deletion?
[03:12] Maya: yes, we have hosted contracts with configurable retention and a private option (VPC/on-prem) for sensitive data. i'll share SOC2 and ISO docs, also SAML/SSO and KMS integration notes. we can set up a short-term policy to not persist raw documents and only keep embeddings for X days, or use customer-managed KMS.
[03:35] Olivia: does hosted support SAML SSO for the Console?
[03:40] Maya: yes, Console supports SAML/SSO + RBAC.
[03:44] Jared: one blocker is procurement - if you have SOC2 plus an in-country data option that's helpful.
[03:50] Maya: noted. i'll attach the whitepapers.
[03:55] [04:00] Samir: jumping back to demo - here is the Console: route definitions, per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown. you can pin a model per route and set fallback policies if the primary is out of capacity. also canary rollouts.
[04:20] Samir: here's an example rerank curl: curl -X POST /v1/rerank -d '{"query":"women's waterproof boot","candidates": [{"id":"p1","text":"..."}, ...] }' returns scores array. we show structured output so you can log features for analysis.
[04:50] Priya: do you support storing embeddings in our VPC or do we have to use your managed store?
[04:55] Samir: hosted defaults to managed vector store; Dedicated/Private options let you keep vectors in your VPC. for hybrid setups we can connect to your s3 / ANN endpoint via private link.
[05:15] Jared: curious about unit costs; any rough numbers for 1M queries/month with avg 8 candidates?
[05:20] Maya: i'll surface exact pricing in the follow-up, but rough hosted estimate: embeddings + rerank per query is dominated by rerank if you use a larger model. Optimize can lower per-query tokens and suggest smaller reranker for candidate scoring. we sent a cost worksheet earlier to illustrate trade-offs.
[05:45] Olivia: do you do A/B experiments in the Console?
[05:48] Samir: yes, route-level A/B and canary rollouts with per-variant analytics and quality metrics. you can hook your eval prompt sets and surface regressions.
[06:05] Jared: any limits on candidate count? we sometimes need top 50 then reprocess.
[06:09] Samir: we support up to 100 candidates, but latency scales linearly; common pattern - retrieve top 50 from ANN and re-rank top 10 for latency-sensitive paths.
[06:25] [06:30] Priya: are there pre-built integrators for ecomm platforms?
[06:32] Maya: we have SDKs and reference connectors, not all ecomm platforms out-of-the-box but we've done shopify and magento reference apps.
[06:40] Jared: competitor question - how is this different vs using Elastic + custom rerank?
[06:45] Samir: main difference: we provide managed neural embeddings + reranker tuned for production at scale, plus Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization). Elastic gives infra + some plugins but you'd still build the rerank model, monitoring, and fallback. we also provide transparent performance profiles so you can predict cost/latency.
[07:10] Olivia: what about vector DB choices? you demoed pinecone, can we plug in our existing faiss cluster?
[07:15] Samir: yes, we interop with FAISS, Pinecone, Milvus, etc. we pass vectors and you control the ANN.
[07:25] Jared: can you run a quick baseline with our sample?
[07:28] Samir: absolutely - if you can share 1k queries + docs we'll run a rerank baseline, we'll need S3 link or secure upload.
[07:35] Jared: i'll share.
[07:37] Maya: recap - we'll send pricing and security docs, samir will run baseline once we get data, and schedule a POC scoping call.
[07:45] Olivia: timeline - procurement wants a two week pilot then decision.
[07:50] Maya: sounds doable; we'll propose pilot scope in the scoping call.
[07:55] [08:00] Jared: couple small follow-ups - what's your SLA for hosted?
[08:03] Maya: standard hosted SLA is 99.9 for API availability; Dedicated has higher uptime and capacity guarantees. specifics in the contract.
[08:15] Priya: do you have models optimized for reranking that are quantized?
[08:18] Samir: yes, Optimize suggests quant profiles and we can run a quantized reranker that reduces latency and memory. sometimes slight accuracy drop but good tradeoff.
[08:35] Olivia: any notes about KV cache, i saw in docs but unclear if it applies to rerank.
[08:40] Samir: KV cache is for autoregressive models to accelerate generation; rerank is pairwise scoring so caching works differently - we cache embeddings and candidate vectors, not KV cache. transcription may sometimes write K V cache as a single token.
[08:55] [09:00] Maya: ok wrapping up - next steps: pricing + security docs, samir baseline, jared to share data, schedule dec 30.
[09:10] Jared: thanks all, good demo.
[09:12] Samir: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
